title: [finding] check-section-landing-index covers 8 docs sections; the three that produced the sitemap-only orphans are outside it
body:
Found while implementing #12353 (four doc pages with no editorial inbound link). Recording, not fixing — the remedy touches body headings, which is epic #12243's declared territory.

## What is covered today

`scripts/check-section-landing-index.mjs` enforces a good rule: a section landing page's index block must enumerate its directory's `meta.json` pages, in `meta.json` order, in both directions. Its own verdict line on `main`:

```
check-section-landing-index: 8 section index block(s) enumerate their meta.json pages, in order, both directions (ai, api, automation, data-modeling, ...)
```

The gate finds its population by looking for the `What's in this module` heading, with `EXPECTED_MIN_SECTIONS = 8` as a shrink-guard floor. A section whose landing page does not carry that heading is not checked at all — it is not a failure, it is simply not in the census.

## Why that matters, measured

`content/docs/kernel/contracts/index.mdx` carries a Contract Catalog table naming all five contracts that have their own page — as plain text, linking none of them. Two of those five (`auth-service`, `cache-service`) had no editorial inbound link from anywhere in `content/docs`, and every gate was green the whole time. `concepts` and `protocol` are in the same position: landing pages with no enumerating block, and one orphaned child page each at the time #12353 was filed.

So the defect class the gate exists to catch is live in the sections the gate does not cover.

## Note on who fixes it

Bringing a section into the census means giving its landing page the `What's in this module` heading — a body heading. Epic #12243 owns frontmatter and body headings under `content/docs/**`, so this is filed for triage rather than fixed alongside the link repair in #12353.

Blocked-by: #12243
